optimization.action_description: Episode 122 closes two false leads with measurement, then ships a bit-identical gated pipeline-depth candidate. CLOSED: (1) HOST OVERHEAD is NOT exposed in the authoritative metric -- end_to_end_time_ms is triton do_bench(warmup=10,rep=100,return_mode=all) median, which brackets one Model.forward behind a 256MB L2 flush; with n_repeat=O(1000s) for small shapes the ~60us host dispatch runs ahead in steady state, so db==kernel GPU time with host HIDDEN for every shape (t1_b1_q64_kv64 db 43us < host 61us). The source _hd256_fastpath replay is also DEAD CODE (cache stored under a 17-tuple _hd256_fast_sig at interface.py:1752 but looked up under a 7-tuple short sig at :1897, never matches; and kernel.py calls _flash_attn_fwd which only populates the cache, never consults it) so fixing it would not move db. (2) exp2 already optimal on sm_103 (hardware ex2, +5-9% shipped). (3) kv_stage swept globally deeper(5,6) and shallower(3,2): kv4 is the robust GLOBAL optimum; depth is a load-bound-vs-fill tradeoff, not a broad lever. CANDIDATE: gate a deeper KV pipeline (kv7) to the load-latency-bound batch1 NON-SPLIT path only (use_dedicated_hd256_kernel AND NOT hd256_split_kv_loads == batch1 & max_seqlen_k<96K, the single-interleaved-load-warp path NCU shows is long_scoreboard-bound 42% / 76% tensor). interface.py only (+36/-2): new _HD256_KVSTAGE_NS knob (default 7), hd256_kv_stage_eff wired into compile_key + kv_stage_override; the compute-bound split path (batch>1/kv>=96K, ~85% tensor) keeps eff=0 -> kernel default 4 -> byte-identical compile (it REGRESSES under depth, b8 +8-10% at kv6/7). EVIDENCE (L20D/sm_103 gateway, runtime cap (10,3) 148 SMs authoritative over the desensitized name; torch 2.9.0+cu130, triton 3.7.1): BIT-IDENTICAL over the complete public domain (54 comparisons=18 shapes x 3 draws: batch1 non-split kv64..90000 + q16384 full-causal, batch1 split kv99000/131072, batch>1 split b2/b4/b8/b16, ragged b3/b4/b16; n_bad=0, worst_maxabs 0.0, all torch.equal; rel_l2 vs immutable reference worst 0.0261<0.05). ABBA (db column, 5 paired blocks, arm order alternated): non-split family +8.07% geomean (best -22.4% b1_q1024_kv8192, -19.2% b1_q1024_kv65536, -7.9% b1_q2048_kv16384; worst changed shape 1.0034=noise), split family -0.21% NEUTRAL (byte-identical, all within the ~+-0.8% noise floor), overall +4.34%, ZERO regressions; ship-defaults smoke (no monkeypatch) confirms the as-committed default IS the candidate. RISK: the win surface is genuinely batch1-non-split-only (the dominant split family is compute-bound and regresses under depth, so it cannot be broadened by this lever); auth geomean ~= +8% x (hidden batch1 non-split fraction), clearing the 1% gate iff that fraction >~12% (4 of 30). It is STRICTLY SAFER than v42 split-for-batch1 (which changed warp structure and measured -0.9% auth): depth adds no warps and never raises time-to-first-MMA (fill=min(depth,blocks)), so no non-split shape can regress and the split family is byte-identical -- the auth floor is neutral, not negative. If the hidden batch1 non-split fraction is too low (the v41/v42 dilution lesson) it dilutes below 1% like them; that is the dominant residual risk.

experiments.name: reconstruct_incumbent_and_decompose_host_vs_device_overhead
experiments.hypothesis: Tree source at HEAD c921ca4 is byte-identical to the episode-116 promoted incumbent (episodes 117-121 committed only memory/vN.json, no source). The authoritative metric is end_to_end_time_ms = triton do_bench(warmup=10,rep=100,return_mode=all) median, which brackets one Model.forward with CUDA events behind a 256MB L2 flush. Hypothesis to test: host-side Python dispatch in _flash_attn_fwd (~60us per the interface.py:88-95 comment) may be EXPOSED in db for small shapes (a broad bit-identical lever), since the source already documents a fast-path replay for exactly this.
experiments.change: Built profiles/e122/probe.py (public-contract, vendor pinned first + flash_attn evicted). Decomposed per-shape time into db (do_bench median, authoritative proxy), dev (cuda-event throughput over 50 back-to-back no-sync calls), and host (perf_counter enqueue cost, no sync) across 13 shapes tiny->extreme. Also read the fast-path internals.
experiments.evidence: HW ground truth: capability (10,3)=sm_103, 148 SMs, smem_optin 232448B, torch 2.9.0+cu130, triton 3.7.1 (desensitized name NVIDIA L20D). host cost is ~60-64us for EVERY shape (full _flash_attn_fwd dispatch). But db < host even for the tiniest shape (t1_b1_q64_kv64: db=43.07us, dev=61.50us, host=60.96us): do_bench 256MB L2 flush (~32us GPU) + huge iteration count (n_repeat=int(100/0.043)=2325 for t1) let the host run ahead in steady state, so db == kernel GPU time with host HIDDEN. CODE: _flash_attn_fwd (interface.py:628, the entry kernel.py calls directly) only POPULATES _HD256_FAST_CACHE (1754/1777); the REPLAY _hd256_fastpath is consulted only at line 3748 inside flash_attn_varlen_func, which kernel.py bypasses. WORSE: the cache is STORED under _hd256_fast_sig (17-tuple incl knobs, line 1752) but LOOKED UP under a 7-tuple short sig (line 1897) -> dict.get never matches -> the fast path is DEAD CODE that never fires even for its intended caller. Confirmed empirically: host stays ~60us for all shapes (no replay).
experiments.result: Host-dispatch reduction is NOT a viable lever for the authoritative metric: db is kernel-GPU-bound (host hidden behind the do_bench flush+iteration count) for every shape including the tiniest. Fixing the dead fast path would cut host 60->~10us but leave db unchanged. This falsifies the interface.py:88-95 premise for the current do_bench protocol and closes the host-overhead direction. db is also COLD-CACHE (L2 flushed): measured cold penalty db-dev is +18% for batch1 non-split (load-bound) but only +5% for batch>1 split (compute-bound, robust). Next: device-side levers only.

experiments.name: kv_stage_global_sweep_deeper_and_shallower_falsified_as_a_global_lever
experiments.hypothesis: db is cold-cache (L2 flushed) so per-tile pipeline fill latency is exposed; kv_stage (KV smem pipeline depth, default 4, knob FA_HD256_KVSTAGE in compile_key line 1340 + kv_stage_override line 1530) is bit-identical. Hypothesis: a deeper pipeline broadly hides the cold fill + dependent page-gather latency; a shallower one might cut fill cost for the many-tile batch>1 family.
experiments.change: Zero source change: same-invocation ABBA via monkeypatching interface._HD256_KVSTAGE (compile_key reads it per call). profiles/e122/kv_sweep.py, authoritative db column (do_bench warmup=10 rep=100 median), 5 paired blocks, balanced 9-shape set weighted to the dominant batch>1 split family. Swept kv_stage 5,6 (deeper) then 3,2 (shallower) vs base 4.
experiments.evidence: DEEPER: only robust monotone win is batch1 NON-SPLIT long-kv (b1_q2048_kv16384: kv5 -5.6%, kv6 -9.6%); batch>1 split deltas inconsistent across kv5/kv6 (m1 +1.4%/+0.05%, l2 +1.6%/-1.0%, b4 +0.8%/+1.7%) = ~+-1.5% noise. Balanced geomean kv5 +0.50%, kv6 +1.18% (driven entirely by the one b1 shape). SHALLOWER: kv3 geomean -2.73%, kv2 -8.63% (b1_q2048_kv16384 +17.4%/+58.6%, b1_q1024_kv131072 +7.8%/+19.5%) - shallower HURTS badly, confirming the non-split path is load-latency-bound. batch>1 shallow was heterogeneous (b4 -4.4% at kv3 but l2 +6.4%), no clean broad win.
experiments.result: kv_stage=4 is a robust GLOBAL optimum; depth is a load-bound-vs-fill tradeoff, not a broad lever. Deeper helps only the batch1 non-split family (single interleaved load warp); shallower hurts it. A per-shape oracle depth would give +2.1% but is an overfitting trap (heterogeneous, misclassification costs up to +6.4%). The actionable finding: gate deeper pipeline to the non-split path only. decision=continue toward that conditional candidate.

experiments.name: depth_sweep_finds_optimal_non_split_depth_and_confirms_split_must_keep_kv4
experiments.hypothesis: If the batch1 non-split path is load-latency-bound, the optimal KV depth for it is >4 and the win grows with depth until smem saturates; the compute-bound batch>1 split path must KEEP kv4 (deeper regresses it), so the depth must be gated to the non-split path.
experiments.change: profiles/e122/depth_b1.py: same-invocation ABBA (interface._HD256_KVSTAGE monkeypatch), db column, 5 paired blocks, 7 batch1 non-split shapes (kv64..kv65536, q64..q4096) + 2 batch>1 split controls, swept kv4/5/6/7/8.
experiments.evidence: All depths 5-8 fit smem (compiled+ran 9/9; smem is shape-independent: kv_stage x fixed K/V stage bytes + Q(q_stage=2) + sO_epi(128x128) + barriers, within the 232448B optin). batch1 NON-SPLIT geomean vs kv4: kv5 +3.71%, kv6 +7.30%, kv7 +8.08%, kv8 +8.15% (plateaus at kv7). Per-shape at kv7: b1_q1024_kv8192 -22.1%, b1_q1024_kv65536 -19.6%, b1_q2048_kv16384 -8.9%, b1_q512_kv4096 -1.4%, b1_q4096_kv32768 -0.7%, tiny b1_q64_kv64/b1_q256_kv2048 neutral (fill=min(depth,blocks)). CONTROLS: split b8_q512_kv4096 REGRESSES with depth (kv5 +3.8%, kv6 +8.2%, kv7 +9.7%) and split b4_q1024_kv8192 is neutral - so deeper must NOT touch the split path.
experiments.result: Optimal non-split depth = kv7 (+8.08% family geomean, essentially tied with kv8 at lower smem). The split path must keep kv4 (deeper regresses the compute-bound dominant family). This dictates a CONDITIONAL depth gated on (use_dedicated_hd256_kernel AND NOT hd256_split_kv_loads) = batch1 & max_seqlen_k<96K. Chose kv7. decision=continue to implement the gated candidate.

experiments.name: implement_gated_deeper_non_split_pipeline_validate_bit_identity_and_abba
experiments.hypothesis: A deeper KV pipeline (kv7) gated to the load-latency-bound batch1 non-split path is bit-identical, strictly no-regression (the split path keeps kv4 byte-identically), and wins ~8% on that family -- a safer bet than v42 split (which changed warp structure and regressed -0.9% auth).
experiments.change: interface.py ONLY (+36/-2): added _HD256_KVSTAGE_NS knob (default 7, env FA_HD256_KVSTAGE_NS, NOT in adapter _STABLE_KNOBS so the source default governs); computed hd256_kv_stage_eff = _HD256_KVSTAGE if >0 else (_HD256_KVSTAGE_NS if use_dedicated_hd256_kernel and not hd256_split_kv_loads and _HD256_KVSTAGE_NS>0 else 0); wired it into the compile_key (was _HD256_KVSTAGE) and the kv_stage_override kwarg. Split path => eff 0 => kernel default 4 => compile_key entry identical to incumbent (byte-identical compile). No kernel-body change.
experiments.evidence: BIT-IDENTITY (profiles/e122/validate.py, fresh vendor import): 54 comparisons = 18 shapes x 3 random draws, candidate(kv7 non-split) vs incumbent arm(_HD256_KVSTAGE_NS=0 => kv4) on the SAME input tensors: n_bad=0, worst_maxabs=0.0, all torch.equal=True. Domain covered: batch1 non-split kv64/2048/4096/8192/16384/32768/65536/90000 + q16384_kv16384 (max total_q full causal); batch1 split kv99000/kv131072; batch>1 split b2/b4/b8/b16; ragged b3/b4/b16 (flatten/LPT). rel_l2 vs immutable reference worst 0.026129 < 0.05 (inc==cand). ABBA (profiles/e122/abba.py, db column, 5 paired blocks, arm order alternated): NON-SPLIT family geomean +8.07% (n=7, worst 1.0034=noise, best 0.7757=-22.4%: b1_q1024_kv8192 -22.4%, b1_q1024_kv65536 -19.2%, b1_q2048_kv16384 -7.9%); SPLIT family geomean -0.21% NEUTRAL (n=6, all within +-0.8%, byte-identical compile); overall +4.34%, overall worst 1.0081 on a BYTE-IDENTICAL split shape (= the ~+-0.8% noise floor, not a regression). SHIP-DEFAULTS smoke (no monkeypatch): _HD256_KVSTAGE_NS=7/_HD256_KVSTAGE=0 confirmed; non-split default(kv7) vs incumbent(kv4) torch.equal=True maxabs 0.0 and 56.26us vs 70.85us (ratio 0.794); split shape is the SAME compile (eff 0 both arms).
experiments.result: PASS on every dev gate: bit-identical over the complete public domain, split path byte-identical and neutral, non-split family +8% with ZERO regressions (worst changed shape within noise). Strictly safer than v42 (no warp-structure change => no regression mode; auth floor is neutral not negative). Auth geomean ~= +8% x (hidden batch1 non-split fraction); clears the 1% gate iff that fraction >~12% (4 of 30). The win surface is genuinely batch1-non-split-only (the dominant batch>1 split family is compute-bound at ~85% tensor and regresses under depth, so it cannot be broadened by this lever). Ship as candidate_ready; the supervisor ABBA on the hidden set is the acceptance authority.

open_directions.direction: The batch1 non-split path is load-latency-bound on the dependent per-KV-block mPageTable[batch,idx] gather feeding each per-page TMA (cutlass.range unroll=1 blocks compiler pipelining). A shallow in-register ROLLING page-table prefetch (depth 2-4, issued before the acquire_and_advance barrier wait so the latency overlaps it) could win MORE on this family than depth alone and without the smem cost -- mechanistically distinct from v42 falsified smem BATCH prefetch (which concentrated latency). Same narrow family.

The dominant batch>1 split family is compute-bound at ~85% tensor and robust to pipeline depth and cold cache; confirm via NCU whether the residual ~14% is the indivisible QK->softmax->PV chain (no lever) or an attackable stall BEFORE spending another episode on the steady-state mainloop.

If the supervisor hidden set has a low batch1 non-split fraction (v42 regressed -0.9% on the same family), the campaign is at a true tuning plateau; the next structural lever is a dedicated low-latency small-shape path -- the tiny shapes are ~40us of fixed GPU launch/fill/epilogue overhead under the cold-cache (L2-flushed) authoritative timer -- not mainloop tuning.

The dead fast-path (sig store/lookup mismatch interface.py:1752 vs :1897; _flash_attn_fwd populates but never consults) is irrelevant to db today (host hidden), but if the authoritative timer ever shrinks the L2 flush or iteration count host dispatch becomes exposed; fixing it plus routing _flash_attn_fwd through a replay honoring the caller-supplied out tensor would then be a broad lever.
